full_judgment: 6. From perusal of the judgments of the courts below I am quite unable to find that the appellate Court has come to a definite finding as to the disobedience of the order of temporary injunction. Rather, from the report of the Process Server it appears that the petitioner cut and took away paddy on 29.7.81. Although in the petition for disobedience the date of cutting paddy was given on 27.7.81. Even if we assume that the petitioner cut the paddy in question on 27.7.81 yet they have done so before service of the order of the court which was served on them on 31.7.81. Thus, not only for want of specific date as to disobedience of the order of temporary injunction as found in the judgments but even on reference to the petition for disobedience alleging the date of disobedience and the report of the process server having had been served on 31.7.81 it appears that the petitioner cut and took away the paddy prior to the service of the order of ad-interim injunction. The contention of Mr. SS Halder in this regard that as the petitioners have filed a case under section 144 CrPC and under section 379 of the Penal Code against the opposite parties the opposite parties shall be deemed to have been in possession of the disputed land. Be that as it may, the question which requires to be adjudicated in the application under Order 39, rule 2(3) is that whether the petitioner committed the offence of disobedience of the court's order. In view of dismissal of the aforesaid two criminal cases, as pointed out by Mr. Halder, it cannot be assumed that the petitioner was not in possession of the disputed property at the time when they cut and took away the paddy. Thus, this contention of Mr. Halder is of no substance.
